reply:
Who they are Zino Aviation is a founder and angel investor based in Nigeria, actively backing pre-seed companies. They typically invest around €3 million and focus on B2B SaaS, enterprise software, fintech and consumer markets. They look for strong technical teams, deep domain expertise, repeat-founder experience or enterprise-sales strength, and are open to regulated businesses. So far This is the first contact. There is no relationship history or prior discussion on record. What they'll likely ask What does Kiln Payroll do, and which problem are you solving? We build payroll and tax compliance software for small and medium businesses in Lagos, Nigeria. We help businesses manage payroll and tax compliance in one place. I should be ready to explain the customer pain, current workflow and why our product is better than existing alternatives. What traction do you have so far? Revenue was NGN 12,000,000 last month and is growing month on month. My record does not show the number of customers, growth rate, retention, churn or revenue breakdown, so I should have those figures ready. Who are your customers, and how do you acquire them? We serve small and medium businesses in Lagos, Nigeria. My record does not show the customer count, customer profile by segment, acquisition channels or sales cycle, so I should answer those directly rather than imply evidence I do not have. Why is this the right team to build the company? My record does not include the founding team's background, technical capability, payroll or tax expertise, or enterprise-sales experience. I should give a concise account of the relevant experience and be clear about any capability we still need to add. What are you looking for from an investor at this stage? I am speaking with you because you back early-stage software and fintech businesses and engage with founders early. I should explain the funding amount, use of funds, current fundraising status and the specific strategic support I would value. Those details are not in my record, so I need to prepare them before the call. Weak spots The traction picture is too thin beyond last month's revenue of NGN 12,000,000 and month-on-month growth. State the revenue figures plainly, then add customer count, month-over-month growth rate, retention, churn, gross margin and pipeline if available. Do not describe growth as strong without the underlying trend. The record does not establish the scale or nature of the customer base, nor how Kiln Payroll wins customers. Explain the target customer, the compliance and payroll pain, acquisition channel, sales cycle and evidence of repeatable demand. If any of these are not yet measured, say so directly. The record does not show the team's relevant experience or the fundraising proposition. Prepare a concise team overview, the amount being raised, use of funds, runway and the specific reason Zino Aviation is a fit. Avoid assuming interest or implying a commitment from a first call. Your ask If there is mutual fit, ask whether Zino Aviation would be open to a follow-up conversation after reviewing the key metrics and fundraising details, and what information they would need to assess Kiln Payroll further. Want to rehearse it? I'll play Zino Aviation.
